# Chapter exercise: Thematic Maps with tmap {.unnumbered}

**People, Cities, and Rivers**

This exercise goes with **Chapter 10, Thematic Maps with tmap**. It builds on the tidyverse exercises from Chapters 6 to 9. It should take you about **one hour**. Read this whole section before you start.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}

## Purpose

**Skills you'll practice.** By the end of this exercise you will be able to:

1. Explain what an sf object is: a data frame of attributes with a geometry column.
2. Build a map in layers with `tm_shape()` and `tm_polygons()`, `tm_dots()`, or `tm_lines()`.
3. Shade features by an attribute, and control the classes with `n` and `style` in `tm_scale_intervals()`.
4. Explain how the choice of classification style changes the story a map tells.
5. Combine several layers in one map, and finish it with a title, a scale bar, a north arrow, and credits.
6. Switch between static and interactive maps with `tmap_mode()`.

**Knowledge you'll gain.** You'll map where people live in the United States, compare a map of population with a map of population *density*, and map the world's largest cities on top of life expectancy.

**Why this matters.** Maps are the main product of spatial data science: they are how you will show your results in every remaining assignment and your final project. A thematic map can tell very different stories depending on what you map (counts or rates) and how you classify it. Learning to make those choices on purpose, and to finish a map so a reader can trust it, is the difference between a map that informs and one that misleads.

## Task

Work through Parts 1 to 7 in order, top to bottom. In each part:

- Read the short explanation, then do each step marked with a bullet (•).
- Wherever you see `___`, replace it with the missing code **before** you run the chunk. A chunk with `___` in it won't run.
- **Before you run** each chunk, picture the map you expect. Then run it and compare.
- Answer each question (**Q1**, **Q2**, ...) in a sentence or two of Markdown, where it says *Your answer here.*
- tmap layers are joined with `+`, like ggplot2. Data steps before `tm_shape()` use the pipe `|>`.

| Part | What you'll do | About |
|:-----|:---------------|:------|
| 1 | Set up your file and look at an sf object | 6 min |
| 2 | Map polygons: population and density | 12 min |
| 3 | Classification: `n` and `style` | 10 min |
| 4 | Map points: the world's largest cities | 8 min |
| 5 | Map lines: the rivers of Paris | 5 min |
| 6 | Put a finished map together | 14 min |
| 7 | Reflect, knit, and turn in | 5 min |

**Turn in** your `.Rmd` file and your knitted `.html` file on Canvas.

## Criteria for success

Use this checklist before you turn your work in. Each item matches a row of the rubric below.

- [ ] The file knits to HTML with no errors, and every map appears in it.
- [ ] Every `___` has been filled in, and every chunk runs.
- [ ] Every question (Q1 to Q11) has an answer in complete sentences that describes what the map shows, with place names.
- [ ] Your finished map in Part 6 has a title, a legend title, a scale bar, a north arrow, and credits with your name and the data source.
- [ ] Your code uses tmap version 4 arguments (`fill =`, `fill.scale =`, `tm_title()`), not the old version 3 ones.
- [ ] The file is back in `tmap_mode("plot")` before it knits.
- [ ] No `install.packages()` line is anywhere in the file.
- [ ] The three reflection questions are answered.

| Criterion | Full credit | Partial credit | No credit |
|:----------|:------------|:---------------|:----------|
| Knits (2 pts) | Knits to HTML with every map showing | Knits, but some chunks have errors | Doesn't knit, or no HTML turned in |
| Map code (5 pts) | Every blank filled in correctly; every map shows what was asked | Most maps correct | Many blanks missing or wrong |
| Questions (8 pts) | Q1 to Q11 answered, describing patterns with place names and reasons | Some answers missing, or vague ("it's darker in places") | Most answers missing |
| Finished map (3 pts) | Title, legend title, scale bar, north arrow, and credits; nothing covers the data | Some parts missing | Not done |
| Style (1 pt) | tmap v4 arguments, `+` between layers, pipe for data steps, no `install.packages()` | | Several problems |
| Reflection (1 pt) | All three answered | | Missing |

**What a good answer looks like.** Here is a question, a weak answer, and a strong one.

> *Question:* Where do the states with the most people cluster?
>
> *Weak answer:* "On the coasts."
>
> *Strong answer:* "The darkest class is California, Texas, Florida, and New York, the four biggest states by population. A second band runs through the Midwest and Northeast (Illinois, Ohio, Pennsylvania). The Mountain West and Great Plains are in the lightest class."

The strong answer names places, says which class they're in, and describes the pattern rather than a single impression.

**IMPORTANT!** Save often. Before you knit, choose **Run > Restart R and Run All Chunks** to make sure every chunk works from a fresh start.
